questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: The table shows the main characteristics of employment in two occupations. occupation X occupation Y average annual wage $100 000 $60 000 number of weeks annual leave 5 weeks 10 weeks average length of working week 48 hours 44 hours job security low high length of training course to obtain job qualification 1 year 2 years What can definitely be deduced from the table?

options.A: Those employed in occupation Y attach greater importance to job security.
options.B: Those employed in occupation X attach less importance to leisure activities.
options.C: There will be more competition for places on training courses to enter occupation X than occupation Y.
options.D: Occupation Y has greater non-pecuniary advantages than occupation X.

questions.questionText: Which diagram correctly shows the relationship between the average product (AP) and the marginal product (MP) of labour given that the quantities of other factor inputs remain constant?

options.A: B MP AP product product AP MP O O labour labour
options.C: D MP AP product product MP AP O O labour labour

questions.questionText: What is the name for the relationship between a firm’s output and the quantities of factor inputs that it employs?

options.B: a long-run production function
options.D: returns to scale

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the supply and demand for labour in an industry. S W wage rate D O L M N employment Initially the industry’s labour market is in equilibrium. What effect will the introduction of a minimum wage OW have on the level of employment in the industry?

options.A: It will decrease by an amount LM.
options.B: It will decrease by an amount LN.
options.C: It will increase by an amount LN.
options.D: It will increase by an amount MN.

questions.questionText: A product with infinite elasticity of supply has sales of 1000 units a week at a price of $1 per unit. Price elasticity of demand is 1.5 over the relevant range. The government imposes a tax of 10%. What will be the government’s weekly tax revenue?
What is the likely outcome for producers and consumers when a market moves from being non-contestable to being a contestable market? producers consumers

options.A: gain from higher prices gain from a wider choice of products
options.B: gain from likely higher profits lose from likely higher prices
options.C: lose from likely lower output lose from a reduced choice of products
options.D: lose from likely lower profits gain from likely lower prices

questions.questionText: A firm is engaging in price discrimination. In order to maximise profits, what should the firm do?

options.A: charge a higher price to consumers earning higher incomes
options.B: charge a higher price to consumers earning lower incomes
options.C: charge a higher price to consumers whose demand for the product is price inelastic
options.D: charge a higher price to consumers whose demand for the product is price elastic

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the private and social marginal costs and benefits at different volumes of traffic. MSC MPC + tax x z MPC costs, y benefits MPB = MSB O volume of traf f i c The imposition of a congestion tax raises the MPC curve to MPC + tax. Which area measures the resulting reduction in the deadweight loss?

options.A: x + y only B x + y + z C y only D z only

questions.questionText: A government imposes a maximum price for electricity. Which statement justifying this measure might be considered valid on economic grounds?

options.A: It will encourage electricity suppliers to invest in additional capacity.
options.B: It will increase the incentive for consumers to conserve energy.
options.C: It will prevent the monopolistic exploitation of consumers.
options.D: It will prevent the rationing of electricity through power cuts.

questions.questionText: Individuals are free to choose the number of hours they work, how much of their income they save and which goods and services they buy. Which type of tax will not distort the choices individuals make?

options.A: a tax levied on the wealth accumulated by individuals
options.B: a uniform tax which raises the same fixed amount from all individuals
options.D: proportional income taxes

questions.questionText: An economy is operating at its natural rate of unemployment. According to monetarist theory, what will be the effect on unemployment in the short run and in the long run of an unanticipated increase in the money supply? short run long run

options.B: no change reduction
options.D: reduction reduction

questions.questionText: What will reduce the value of the investment multiplier?

options.A: a low marginal propensity to import
options.B: automatic stabilisers
options.D: low rates of unemployment benefit

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what will result in a decrease in aggregate demand?

options.B: a decrease in the balance of trade deficit
options.C: a decrease in the government’s budget deficit
options.D: a decrease in the household saving ratio

questions.questionText: What will expand the money supply in an open economy?

options.A: a current account balance of payments deficit
options.B: an increase in the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks
options.D: government intervention to prevent an appreciation in the foreign exchange value of domestic currency

options.B: constant increase decrease
options.D: increase increase increase

options.B: high low
options.D: high high

questions.questionText: Which cause of economic growth would involve the least cost for present and future generations of a country’s population?

options.A: increased exploitation of a country’s mineral resources
options.B: investment financed by borrowing from abroad
options.C: investment financed by high rates of domestic savings
options.D: technological innovations in productive processes

options.B: a lower expected rate of inflation

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a government’s revenue and expenditure for three years. revenue expenditure revenue expenditure revenue expenditure 0 1 2 3 4 $m What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: A budget deficit was replaced by a budget surplus.
options.B: A government borrowing requirement emerged.
options.C: The economy moved from a recession into a boom period.
options.D: The yield from taxation continuously increased.

questions.questionText: Which tax is most likely to be regressive?

options.B: a property tax
options.D: income tax

questions.questionText: Why might a reduction in domestic interest rates have an adverse effect on a country’s balance of payment on current account?

options.A: It will cause a rise in the exchange rate.
options.B: It will make the country’s industry less competitive.
options.C: The resulting higher level of economic activity is likely to increase imports.
options.D: There will be an outflow of capital from the country.

questions.questionText: What would be classified as a supply side policy measure?

options.A: additional legislation to restrict the power of trade unions
options.B: a reduction in the government’s fiscal deficit
options.C: an open market sale of securities
options.D: the imposition of a tariff on imported goods

questions.questionText: A country decides to join a group of countries which maintain fixed parities for their currencies and forbid any restriction on foreign trade and payments. What will the country have to forgo to maintain a fixed parity for its currency?

options.B: an independent fiscal policy
options.D: an independent prices and incomes policy

questions.questionText: What would be an economic benefit to a major economy of imposing a tariff on imported goods?

options.B: It would increase pressure on foreign suppliers to reduce their prices.
options.C: It would make the country’s exports more competitive.
options.D: It would reduce the prices paid by consumers for imported goods.
